key_insight: Retention-constrained fine-tuning improves an aluminium MACE potential’s defect predictions while preserving its tested near-equilibrium mechanical and vibrational response.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports more reliable atomistic simulations of aluminium defect dynamics and plasticity without sacrificing tested bulk-response accuracy.
method: Use conditional readout force uncertainty to acquire configurations, updating covariance within each batch.
Iteratively update all model parameters with relative-energy anchoring to limit loss of historical accuracy.
Gate candidate updates against historical energy and vibrational tolerances.
evidence_signal: After 32 acquisitions and 400 gradient updates, mean development force error fell from 22.43 to 21.52 meV/Å, outperforming comparison strategies; all three force-uncertainty runs met bulk-retention criteria, with harmonic phonon RMS drift below 0.05 THz.
watch_item: Retention is demonstrated only for the tested aluminium configurations and tolerances; new deformation regimes require additional validation.
paper_title: Retention-constrained fine-tuning of a pre-trained aluminium MACE potential for non-equilibrium defect dynamics and plasticity
